translations.title: How can one physics controller accept full trajectories, VR head/hands, arbitrary joint keyframes, and text?
translations.answer: MaskedMimic first trains a physics tracker with complete future goals, then uses DAgger, structured random masking, and a conditional VAE to unify multiple inputs as an explicit partial-goal inpainting interface. It covers only trained mask/condition distributions and does not automatically solve conflicting goals, long-horizon planning, sensor bias, or real-robot deployment.
translations.applicability.assumptions.0: A fully constrained teacher can track the source motion distribution.
translations.applicability.assumptions.1: Deployment command/missingness patterns are represented by the versioned structured-mask distribution.
translations.applicability.environments.0: Simulated full-body, VR, keyframe, text, terrain, and object-conditioned character control
translations.applicability.robots.0: Simulated humanoid characters in the paper; real robots require separate dynamics and safety evidence
translations.applicability.simulators.0: ProtoMotions-supported simulation with matched scene, mask, and observation contracts
translations.confidence_rationale: The two-stage derivation, cross-modality tables, and structured-mask/residual-prior ablations support the interface claim, while pinned official code exposes the relevant mask/model paths. Confidence is capped because compute is large, some modalities have explicit limitations, and all evidence is simulated-character control.
translations.evidence.0.note: Defines teacher-to-partial-goal distillation and shows dense/sparse/multimodal results plus decisive structured-mask and prior ablations.
